stem: In a histogram constructed for a frequency distribution with equal class widths, which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between the height of a bar and the frequency of the corresponding class?

options.text: The height of each bar is directly proportional to the frequency of the class.
The height of each bar is directly proportional to the cumulative frequency of the class.
The height of each bar equals the frequency density (frequency divided by class width).
The height of each bar is directly proportional to the square root of the frequency.

per_option_rationale.rationale: When class widths are equal, frequency density = frequency / h is proportional to frequency (h is constant), so bar height is proportional to frequency.
Confusing a histogram with an ogive (cumulative frequency graph). Histogram bars represent class frequencies, not cumulative frequencies.

While frequency density is the technically general definition for unequal class widths, for equal class widths, height is proportional to frequency, not equal to frequency density in the general case. The key word is equal class widths makes option 1 the specific correct answer here.
No standard statistical representation uses the square root of frequency for bar heights in a histogram.

explanation: For a histogram with equal class widths, frequency density = frequency / class width. Since class width is constant, frequency density is directly proportional to frequency. So bar height is proportional to frequency.

explanation_sections.punchline: Equal class widths: bar height is proportional to frequency (constant denominator makes density proportional to frequency).
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: histogram properties with equal class widths. Decisive move: recall that histogram bar height technically represents frequency density (f/h). When h is constant for all classes, f/h is proportional to f, so heights are proportional to frequencies. Contrast with unequal class widths where you must use density.
explanation_sections.lesson: Histogram bar heights represent frequencies (for equal class widths) or frequency densities (for unequal widths). Never use cumulative frequencies - that is an ogive.
explanation_sections.timing: 25 seconds. Recall the distinction. Trap: option 3 is technically the general definition but option 1 is the specific correct answer for equal class widths.
